correctness.rationale: Evaluating the weight-zero Rota–Baxter identity on basis pairs (t²,t²),(1,t²),(t,t),(1,1) successively forces P(t²)=0, P(t)=ct² and P(1)=at+bt² with a²=2ac; six unordered basis pairs establish sufficiency. P²(1)=ac t² and P³=0. In char2 a=0 yielding q² maps; for odd char the union of planes a=0 and a=2c intersects in q points, giving 2q²−q and q(q−1) maps with P²≠0. Every algebra automorphism maps t↦ut+vt² (u≠0), inducing (a,b,c)↦(ua,u²b+av,uc). When a=0,c≠0, the invariant b/c² runs over q classes; a=c=0 contributes one zero plus |Fq* /(Fq*)²| nonzero square classes; a≠0 contributes one additional class only in odd char, yielding q+2 (even) and q+4 (odd). Independent reimplementation exhaustively tested ALL q^9 endomorphisms for q=2,3 (4 and 15 valid) and rebuilt the orbit groups (4,7), matching formulas; source verifier also checks q=4 in full and q=5 candidates, but no unwarranted claim that this independent checker repeated F4 enumeration.

value.rationale: The first unital one-generator local algebra with nonzero radical square is a natural minimal model for weight-zero Rota–Baxter classification. The arbitrary-characteristic operator structure, stark char2 versus odd index-three nilpotency distinction, and exact conjugacy-orbit spectrum over every finite field describe intrinsic moduli, not just reproducibility of a known char0 list. Though the complex parameter form is old, the finite-field orbit problem is independently motivated and nontrivial enough to be useful as a benchmark for higher truncations.
residual_risks: No claim of novel char0 normal form; contributions are arithmetic/all-field and orbit refinements.
No extension to higher truncations or weight one.

final_claim: All weight-zero Rota–Baxter operators P on unital A=k[t]/(t³), over every field, are P(1)=at+bt², P(t)=ct², P(t²)=0 with a(a−2c)=0. Over F_q there are q² (even char) or q(2q−1) (odd char), and q+2 / q+4 automorphism-conjugacy orbits respectively; all P³=0 and P²≠0 only in odd characteristic with q(q−1) maps.
limitations: Exactly the unital k[t]/t³, weight zero; not higher truncations.
